Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 38, verses 1–11:

Volume seven of Taysir al-Karim al-Mannan fi Tafsir Ayat al-Qur'an
By its compiler Abd al-Rahman ibn Nasir ibn Abd Allah al-Sa'di, may God forgive him, his parents, and all Muslims

It is a Meccan surah.

{1} This is a statement from God Most High about the state of the Qur'an and the state of those who deny it, together with it and with the one who brought it. He says: ﴿Sad. By the Qur'an, full of reminder.﴾ That is: possessing great worth and nobility, reminding the servants of everything they need to know: knowledge of God's names, attributes and acts; knowledge of God's legal rulings; and knowledge of the rulings concerning the return and the recompense. It reminds them of the foundations of their religion and its branches. Here there is no need to mention what is sworn to, for the reality of the matter is that what is sworn by and what is sworn to are one thing, namely this Qur'an described with this sublime description.

{2} Since the Qur'an has this description, it is known that the servants' need for it is greater than every need, and it was obligatory for them to receive it with faith and assent, and to be eager to extract from it that by which they may be reminded. God guided whom He guided to this, but the disbelievers refused it and refused the one who sent it down, and there came to be with them ʿizzah (arrogance) and shiqaq (opposition): ʿizzah meaning refusal to believe in it and haughtiness, and shiqaq meaning hostility and enmity in rejecting it, annulling it, and disparaging the one who brought it.

{3} So He threatened them with the destruction of the earlier generations who denied the messengers, and that when destruction came upon them they cried out and sought relief to turn away the punishment from them, but ﴿there is no escape now﴾. That is: the time is not a time for deliverance from what they have fallen into, nor is there any relief for what has befallen them. So let these people beware of persisting in their arrogance and opposition, lest what befell those (peoples) befall them.

{4} ﴿And they marvel that a warner has come to them from among themselves.﴾ That is: these deniers marvelled at a matter that is not an object of marvel, that a warner came to them from among themselves, so that they could receive from him and know him truly; and because he is of their own people, tribal pride should not hold them back from following him. This is something that makes it obligatory for them to be thankful and to submit fully to him. But they reversed the matter, marvelling with the marvel of denial, and said, out of their disbelief and wrongdoing: ﴿This is a lying sorcerer!﴾

{5} And his offence in their eyes was that ﴿he has made the gods into one god﴾. That is: how can he forbid taking partners and equals and command sincere worship of God alone? ﴿Indeed, this is a thing to be wondered at﴾: that which he brought is something to be marvelled at for its falsehood and corruption in their eyes.

{6} ﴿And the chiefs among them went forth﴾: those whose word is accepted, urging their people to hold fast to the polytheism they were upon. ﴿Walk on, and be steadfast in your gods﴾; that is: persist in them, and strive against your souls to be patient in them and in worshipping them, and let no one turn you back from them, and let no one divert you from their worship. ﴿Indeed, this is a thing that is intended﴾: that which Muhammad brought of forbidding their worship is ﴿a thing that is intended﴾, that is, sought; that is, he has an aim and an intention not sound in that. This is a doubt that passes only over fools, for whoever calls to a word, true or untrue, his word is not rejected by disparaging his intention; his intention and his work are for himself. It is rejected only by confronting it with proofs and demonstrations that nullify and corrupt it. Their intention was that Muhammad called you to what he called you to only so that he might lead among you and be honoured and obeyed among you.

{7} ﴿We have not heard of this﴾: the saying he uttered and the religion to which he called, ﴿in the last religion﴾; that is, in the last time. So our fathers did not reach it, nor did our fathers reach their fathers upon it; so continue upon what your fathers passed upon, for it is the truth. This that Muhammad called to is nothing but a fabrication he invented and a lie he forged. This too is a doubt of the same kind as their first doubt, in that they rejected the truth with something that is not a proof, to reject even the lowest saying, namely that it is a saying contrary to what their misguided fathers were upon. Where, then, in this is anything that indicates its falsehood?

{8} ﴿Has the reminder been sent down to him from among us?﴾ That is: what distinguished him above us, that the reminder should be sent down to him rather than to us, and that God should single him out for it? This too is a doubt, and where is the proof in it against what he said? Are not all the messengers only of this description? God bestows His messengership upon them and commands them to call the creation to God. For this reason, since these statements issuing from them are not fit to refute what the Messenger brought, God informed of their source, and that they are ﴿in doubt about My reminder﴾: they possess no knowledge and no clear evidence. When they fell into doubt, were content with it, and the manifest truth came to them while they were resolved to persist in their doubt, they said what they said of those sayings to repel the truth, not out of clear evidence concerning their affair, but this is merely by way of fabrication on their part. It is known that whoever is of this character speaks out of doubt and obstinacy, so his saying is not accepted, nor does it detract in the slightest from the truth, and blame and reproach are directed at him by the mere fact of his speech. For this reason He threatened them with punishment, saying: ﴿Rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment﴾; that is: they said these sayings and grew bold in them because they were given enjoyment in this world and no punishment from God had touched them. Had they tasted His punishment, they would not have been so bold.

{9} ﴿Or do they possess the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower?﴾ So that they might give to whom they wish and withhold from whom they wish, since they said: ﴿Has the reminder been sent down to him from among us?﴾ That is: this is God's bounty and His mercy, and it is not in their hands, so that they should be bold toward God.

{10} ﴿Or do they have the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them?﴾ So that they would be able to do whatever they wish. ﴿Then let them ascend by the means﴾ that lead them to the heaven, so that they might cut off mercy from the Messenger of God! How can they speak when they are the weakest and most incapable of God's creation, with what they have said?

{11} Or is their aim to form factions, mobilise, and cooperate to support falsehood and forsake the truth? That is indeed what is happening; yet this aim will not be accomplished for them. Rather, their effort is fruitless and their army is routed. For this He said: ﴿A host there, routed, of the factions.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 38, verses 12–15:

{12–15} He, exalted is He, warns them that He may do to them what He did to the nations before them, those who were greater than them in strength and who banded together in falsehood. {The people of Noah, and 'Ad}: the people of Hud; {and Pharaoh, lord of the stakes}; that is, the great armies and the immense power. {And Thamud}: the people of Salih. {And the people of Lot, and the companions of the Thicket}; that is, the trees and the dense gardens, and they were the people of Shu'ayb. {Those are the confederates}: those who gathered together with their strength, their numbers and their equipment to reject the truth, but it availed them nothing. {Each of them}: of these {only denied the messengers, so My punishment}: from God {was justly deserved}. And these, what is it that would purify them and make them pure, so that what befell those would not befall them? So let them await {one blast, for which there is no recovery}; that is, no return or reversal, which will destroy them and uproot them if they persist in what they are upon.

{27} He (Exalted is He) informs of the completeness of His wisdom in His creation of the heavens and the earth, and that He did not create them {in vain} (bāṭilan), i.e., purposelessly and in play, without any benefit or wise purpose. {That is the assumption of those who disbelieve} (ẓann alladhīna kafarū): regarding their Lord, in that they assumed what is not fitting to His majesty. {So woe to those who disbelieve, from the Fire} (fa-waylun lilladhīna kafarū min al-nār): for it is the one that takes from them what is due and reaches them to every extent. Indeed, Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth and for truth. He created them so that the servants might know the perfection of His knowledge, His power, and the vastness of His dominion, and that He, Exalted is He, alone is the One worthy of worship, rather than those who did not create even an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth; and that the Resurrection is true, and that Allah will distinguish between the people of goodness and the people of evil. The one ignorant of the wisdom of Allah would not assume that Allah would equate the two in His judgment.

Section
Concerning what has become clear to us of the benefits and lessons in the story of David and Solomon, peace be upon them.

Among them: Allah, the Exalted, relates to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) the reports of those before him, in order to strengthen his heart and reassure his soul, and He mentions to him their acts of worship, the intensity of their patience, and their turning (to Allah), which inspires him to compete with them, to draw near to Allah through what they drew near to Him, and to endure the harm of his people. For this reason, in this passage, when Allah mentioned the harm his people caused him, their words about him and about what he brought, He commanded him to be patient, and to remember His servant David so that he might be consoled by him.

Among them: Allah, the Exalted, praises and loves strength in His obedience—strength of heart and body—for from it arise the effects of obedience, its goodness and abundance, which do not arise with weakness and lack of strength. The servant should pursue its causes and not incline to laziness and idleness, which weaken strength and enfeeble the soul.

Among them: returning to Allah in all matters is one of the attributes of the prophets of Allah and His elect creation, as Allah praised David and Solomon for it; so let those who seek guidance follow them, and let those who travel the path be guided by their guidance: {Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance}.

Among them: the beautiful, mighty voice with which Allah honored His Prophet David, peace be upon him, through which Allah made the hard mountains and the birds respond to him when he chanted his praise, and they glorified (Allah) along with him in the evening and at sunrise.

Among them: one of the greatest blessings of Allah upon His servant is that He grants him beneficial knowledge and enables him to know judgment and the decision between people, as Allah bestowed this favour upon His servant David, peace be upon him.

Among them: the care of Allah for His prophets and chosen ones when some lapse occurs from them, by testing them and afflicting them with that by which the harm is removed from them and they return to a state more perfect than their former one, as happened to David and Solomon, peace be upon them.

Among them: the prophets, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, are protected from error in what they convey from Allah, the Exalted, because the purpose of prophethood is not achieved without that; and some of the demands of human nature may occur from them in the form of sins, but Allah corrects them and hastens to them with His kindness.

Among them: David, peace be upon him, for most of his time was devoted to his sanctuary (mihrab) in service to his Lord. For this reason the two litigants climbed over the wall of the sanctuary to him, because when he was alone in his sanctuary no one would come to him. He did not devote all his time to the people despite the many judgments that came to him, but set aside a time in which he was alone with his Lord, and his eye was comforted by his worship, and which helped him to be sincere in all his affairs.

Among them: it is necessary to observe good manners when entering upon rulers and others; for when the two litigants entered upon David in an unusual manner and not through the customary door, he was alarmed by them, and it greatly troubled him, seeing it as unbecoming to the situation.

Among them: the harsh conduct of the disputant does not prevent the judge from ruling with the truth.

Among them: the perfect forbearance of David, peace be upon him; for he did not become angry with them when they came to him without permission, though he was the king, nor did he rebuke or reprimand them.

Among them: the permissibility for the wronged person to say to the one who wronged him: "You have wronged me," or "O wrongdoer!" and similar words, or "one who transgresses against me!" based on their statement: {Two adversaries, one of us has wronged the other}.

Among them: that the one being admonished and advised, even if he is of great rank and lofty knowledge, when someone advises him or exhorts him, should not become angry or recoil, but should promptly accept it with gratitude; for the two litigants advised David, and he did not recoil, did not become angry, and this did not turn him away from the truth, but he ruled with pure truth.

Among them: mixing among relatives and companions and the great number of worldly financial attachments causes enmity among them and the transgression of some against others; and nothing restrains from this except using the piety of Allah and patience in affairs through faith and righteous deeds; and this is among the least of things among people.

Among them: seeking forgiveness and worship, especially prayer, are expiations for sins; for Allah linked the forgiveness of David's sin to his seeking forgiveness and his prostration.

Among them: Allah's honouring of His servants David and Solomon with nearness to Him and good reward; and one should not think that what happened to them diminishes their rank before Allah, the Exalted. This is part of the completeness of His kindness to His sincere servants: when He forgives them and removes the effect of their sins, He removes all the consequences that follow from it, even what falls into the hearts of creatures; for when they learn of some of their sins, there falls into their hearts a lowering of their former rank. Allah, the Exalted, removes these effects, and that is not difficult for the Generous, the Forgiving.

Among them: judgment between people is a religious office entrusted to the messengers of Allah and His elect creation, and the duty of one who holds it is to judge with truth and to avoid desire; judging with truth requires knowledge of the legal matters and knowledge of the reality of the case being judged and how to fit it into the legal ruling; so one who is ignorant of either matter is not fit to judge, and it is not lawful for him to undertake it.

Among them: the judge should beware of desire and keep it constantly in mind, for souls are never free of it; rather, he should strive against his own self so that the truth is his aim, and at the time of judgment he should set aside any love or hatred for either litigant.

Among them: Solomon, peace be upon him, is among the virtues of David and among the favours of Allah upon him, in that He granted him to him; and among the greatest blessings of Allah upon His servant is that He grants him a righteous child; for if he is a scholar, he is light upon light.

Among them: Allah's praise and commendation of Solomon in His saying: {How excellent a servant! Indeed he was ever turning (to Allah)}.

Among them: the abundance of Allah's goodness and kindness toward His servants, that He bestows upon them righteous deeds and noble character, and then praises them for it; and He is the Bounteous, the Bestower.

Among them: Solomon's giving precedence to the love of Allah, the Exalted, over the love of everything else.

Among them: that everything that preoccupies the servant from Allah is ill-omened and blameworthy; so let him abandon it and turn to what is more beneficial for him.

Among them: the well-known principle: whoever leaves something for the sake of Allah, Allah will compensate him with something better. Solomon, peace be upon him, slaughtered the swift, beloved horses, giving precedence to the love of Allah, so Allah compensated him with something better than that: He subjected to him the gentle, soft wind that moves at his command wherever he wished and intended, its morning journey being a month and its evening journey a month; and He subjected to him the devils, those capable of works that human beings cannot accomplish.

Among them: that the subjugation of the devils is not granted to anyone after Solomon, peace be upon him.

Among them: that Solomon, peace be upon him, was a king and a prophet, who did what he willed, yet he willed only justice; unlike the prophet-servant, whose will follows the command of Allah, so he does not act or refrain except by command, as is the state of our Prophet (ﷺ); and this state is more perfect.

Among them: Solomon's giving precedence to the love of Allah, the Exalted, over the love of everything else.

For this reason He said: {And indeed for him with Us is a near position and a good return}; that is, he is among those brought near to Allah, honored by Allah with various kinds of noble favours.

Among them: one of the greatest blessings of Allah upon His servant is that He grants him beneficial knowledge and enables him to know judgment and the decision between people, as Allah bestowed this favour upon His servant David, peace be upon him.

Among them: the care of Allah for His prophets and chosen ones when some lapse occurs from them, by testing them and afflicting them with that by which the harm is removed from them and they return to a state more perfect than their former one, as happened to David and Solomon, peace be upon them.

Among them: the prophets, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, are protected from error in what they convey from Allah, the Exalted, because the purpose of prophethood is not achieved without that; and some of the demands of human nature may occur from them in the form of sins, but Allah corrects them and hastens to them with His kindness.

Among them: David, peace be upon him, for most of his time was devoted to his sanctuary (mihrab) in service to his Lord. For this reason the two litigants climbed over the wall of the sanctuary to him, because when he was alone in his sanctuary no one would come to him. He did not devote all his time to the people despite the many judgments that came to him, but set aside a time in which he was alone with his Lord, and his eye was comforted by his worship, and which helped him to be sincere in all his affairs.

Among them: it is necessary to observe good manners when entering upon rulers and others; for when the two litigants entered upon David in an unusual manner and not through the customary door, he was alarmed by them, and it greatly troubled him, seeing it as unbecoming to the situation.

Among them: the harsh conduct of the disputant does not prevent the judge from ruling with the truth.

Among them: the perfect forbearance of David, peace be upon him; for he did not become angry with them when they came to him without permission, though he was the king, nor did he rebuke or reprimand them.

Among them: the permissibility for the wronged person to say to the one who wronged him: "You have wronged me," or "O wrongdoer!" and similar words, or "one who transgresses against me!" based on their statement: {Two adversaries, one of us has wronged the other}.

Among them: that the one being admonished and advised, even if he is of great rank and lofty knowledge, when someone advises him or exhorts him, should not become angry or recoil, but should promptly accept it with gratitude; for the two litigants advised David, and he did not recoil, did not become angry, and this did not turn him away from the truth, but he ruled with pure truth.

Among them: mixing among relatives and companions and the great number of worldly financial attachments causes enmity among them and the transgression of some against others; and nothing restrains from this except using the piety of Allah and patience in affairs through faith and righteous deeds; and this is among the least of things among people.

Among them: seeking forgiveness and worship, especially prayer, are expiations for sins; for Allah linked the forgiveness of David's sin to his seeking forgiveness and his prostration.

Among them: Allah's honouring of His servants David and Solomon with nearness to Him and good reward; and one should not think that what happened to them diminishes their rank before Allah, the Exalted. Among them: the judge should beware of desire and keep it constantly in mind, for souls are never free of it; rather, he should strive against his own self so that the truth is his aim, and at the time of judgment he should set aside any love or hatred for either litigant.

Among them: Solomon, peace be upon him, is among the virtues of David and among the favours of Allah upon him, in that He granted him to him; and among the greatest blessings of Allah upon His servant is that He grants him a righteous child; for if he is a scholar, he is light upon light.

Among them: Allah's praise and commendation of Solomon in His saying: {How excellent a servant! Indeed he was ever turning (to Allah)}.

Among them: the abundance of Allah's goodness and kindness toward His servants, that He bestows upon them righteous deeds and noble character, and then praises them for it; and He is the Bounteous, the Bestower.

Among them: Solomon's giving precedence to the love of Allah, the Exalted, over the love of everything else.

Among them: that everything that preoccupies the servant from Allah is ill-omened and blameworthy; so let him abandon it and turn to what is more beneficial for him.

Among them: the well-known principle: whoever leaves something for the sake of Allah, Allah will compensate him with something better. Solomon, peace be upon him, slaughtered the swift, beloved horses, giving precedence to the love of Allah, so Allah compensated him with something better than that: He subjected to him the gentle, soft wind that moves at his command wherever he wished and intended, its morning journey being a month and its evening journey a month; and He subjected to him the devils, those capable of works that human beings cannot accomplish.

Among them: that the subjugation of the devils is not granted to anyone after Solomon, peace be upon him.

Among them: that Solomon, peace be upon him, was a king and a prophet, who did what he willed, yet he willed only justice; unlike the prophet-servant, whose will follows the command of Allah, so he does not act or refrain except by command, as is the state of our Prophet (ﷺ); and this state is more perfect.

{30} When God praised David and mentioned what happened to him and from him, He praised his son Solomon, peace be upon them both, saying: {And We gave to David Solomon}; that is, We bestowed him upon him and gladdened his eye with him. {How excellent a servant}: Solomon, peace be upon him, for he possessed what calls for praise, which is {indeed he was ever turning (to Allah)} (awwab); that is, returning to Allah in all his circumstances, through devotion (ta'alluh), turning in repentance (inabah), love, remembrance, supplication, humility, and striving to seek Allah's pleasure and to give it precedence over everything.

{31–33} For this reason, when there were displayed before him the swift, well-bred horses {al-safinat} (those whose description includes al-sufun, which is lifting one of their forelegs when standing still; they had a delightful appearance and a wondrous beauty, especially to one who needed them, such as kings), he kept them on display until the sun set behind the veil, and they distracted him from the evening prayer and from his remembrance (of Allah). So he said, in regret for what had passed from him and seeking nearness to Allah through what had distracted him from His remembrance, and giving precedence to the love of Allah over the love of other than Him: {Indeed, I have preferred the love of good}: and "ahbabtu" was used with the meaning of "athartu" (I preferred); that is, I preferred the love of good, which is wealth in general, and in this context it means the horses, {over the remembrance of my Lord until they were hidden by the veil. Bring them back to me}: so they were brought back, {and he began to pass his hand over (their) legs and necks}; that is, he began to slaughter them with his sword at their legs and necks.

{34} {And We certainly tested Solomon}; that is, We afflicted and tried him by the loss of his kingdom and his separation from it, due to a lapse prompted by human nature. {And We placed upon his throne a body}; that is, a devil, whom Allah had decreed and destined to sit on the throne of his kingdom and to exercise authority over the kingdom during the period of Solomon's trial. {Then he turned back}: Solomon turned back to Allah, the Exalted, and repented.

{35–39} So {He said: "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower."}: Allah responded to him, forgave him, returned his kingdom to him, and increased it with a kingship that was not granted to anyone after him: the subjugation of the devils to him, who built whatever he wished and dived for him in the sea, extracting pearls and ornaments; and whoever of them disobeyed him, he bound in chains and fettered. And We said to him: {This is Our gift}: so let him be content with it, {so grant (favours) or withhold}: to whomever you wish, {without account}; that is, there is no blame upon you in that, nor any reckoning, because of Allah's perfect knowledge of His complete justice and the excellence of His judgments.

{40} And do not think that this was for Solomon only in this world, to the exclusion of the Hereafter; rather, in the Hereafter he has a great good. For this reason He said: {And indeed for him with Us is a near position and a good return}; that is, he is among those brought near to Allah, honored by Allah with various kinds of noble favours.

Among them: the abundance of Allah's goodness and kindness toward His servants, that He bestows upon them righteous deeds and noble character, and then praises them for it; and He is the Bounteous, the Bestower.

Among them: Solomon's giving precedence to the love of Allah, the Exalted, over the love of everything else.

Among them: that everything that preoccupies the servant from Allah is ill-omened and blameworthy; so let him abandon it and turn to what is more beneficial for him.

{35–39} So {He said: "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower."}: Allah responded to him, forgave him, returned his kingdom to him, and increased it with a kingship that was not granted to anyone after him: the subjugation of the devils to him, who built whatever he wished and dived for him in the sea, extracting pearls and ornaments; and whoever of them disobeyed him, he bound in chains and fettered. And We said to him: {This is Our gift}: so let him be content with it, {so grant (favours) or withhold}: to whomever you wish, {without account}; that is, there is no blame upon you in that, nor any reckoning, because of Allah's perfect knowledge of His complete justice and the excellence of His judgments.

{40} And do not think that this was for Solomon only in this world, to the exclusion of the Hereafter; rather, in the Hereafter he has a great good. For this reason He said: {And indeed for him with Us is a near position and a good return}; that is, he is among those brought near to Allah, honored by Allah with various kinds of noble favours.

So ﴿he called upon his Lord﴾, supplicating and complaining to Him alone, not to anyone else, saying: "My Lord, ﴿indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment﴾"; that is, with a matter that is burdensome, exhausting, and painful. Satan had been given power over his body, and he blew upon it until it became ulcerated and then festered after that, and his condition grew severe. Likewise, his family and his wealth were destroyed.

Allah enriched him and gave him great wealth, ﴿as a mercy from Us﴾ toward Our servant Ayyub, because he endured patiently, so We rewarded him from Our mercy with a reward both immediate and deferred. ﴿And a reminder for those of understanding﴾; that is, so that people of intellect may remember the state of Ayyub, reflect, and know that whoever endures harm, Allah the Exalted will reward him with an immediate and a deferred reward, and will answer his supplication when he calls upon Him.

{48} That is: mention these prophets with the best of mention, and praise them with the best of praise; for each of them is among the good ones whom Allah chose from among creation, and for whom He chose the most perfect states in deeds, character, praiseworthy attributes and upright qualities.

{49} This: that is, the mention of these chosen prophets and the mention of their attributes, {ذِكۡرٌ} ("a reminder"): in this Qur'an, which is full of reminders, those who remember are reminded by their circumstances, those who seek to follow them yearn to emulate their praiseworthy attributes, and one comes to know what Allah bestowed upon them of pure qualities and what praise He spread for them among mankind. This is one kind of remembrance, namely the remembrance of the people of goodness.

Among the kinds of remembrance is the remembrance of the reward of the people of goodness and the people of evil, and for this reason He said:

{وإنَّ للمتقين} ("Indeed, for the God-fearing"): their Lord, by carrying out the commands and avoiding the prohibitions, from every believing man and woman, {لَحُسۡنَ مآبٍ} ("is an excellent place of return"); that is, a good destination (ma'ab) and a commendable place of return.

{48} That is: mention these Prophets with the best of mention, and praise them with the best of praise; for each of them is among the righteous whom Allah chose from among creation, and He chose for them the most perfect states of deeds, character, praiseworthy attributes and sound qualities.

{49} "This" — that is, the mention of these chosen Prophets and the mention of their attributes — {is a reminder}: in this Qur'an, which is full of reminder. Those who remember are reminded by their circumstances, those who follow aspire to emulate their praiseworthy attributes, and one comes to know what Allah bestowed upon them of pure qualities and what praise He spread for them among creation. This is one kind of remembrance, namely the remembrance of the people of goodness.

Among the kinds of remembrance is the remembrance of the recompense of the people of goodness and the people of evil, and for this He said:

{And indeed, for the God-fearing} — who are dutiful to their Lord by carrying out the commands and avoiding the prohibitions, every believing man and woman — {is an excellent place of return}; that is, a good place of return and a commendable destination.

{50} Then He explained and detailed it, saying: {Gardens of Eden} — that is, gardens of permanent residence, whose owner does not desire any substitute for them because of their perfection and the completeness of their bliss; and they will not be expelled from them nor will they be made to leave. {With their gates opened for them} — that is, the gates of their mansions and dwellings are opened on their behalf; they do not need to open them themselves, rather they are attended to. This is also evidence of complete security, and that there is nothing in the Gardens of Eden that would necessitate that their gates be closed on account of it.

{51} {Reclining therein} — upon adorned couches and ornate sitting places. {Calling therein} — that is, they command their servants to bring {abundant fruit and drink}, of every kind that their souls desire and their eyes delight in. This indicates the perfection of bliss, the perfection of comfort and tranquility, and the completeness of pleasure.

{52} {And with them} — from their spouses, the wide-eyed maidens (ḥūr ʿīn) — {restraining their gaze} to their husbands, and their husbands' gaze is restrained to them, because of the beauty of all of them and each one's love for the other and the absence of any aspiration toward others, and that neither seeks a substitute for his companion nor an exchange for him. {Of equal age} — that is, of one age, the most balanced, best and most delightful age of youth.

{53} {This is what you are promised} — O God-fearing ones — {for the Day of Reckoning}: a recompense for your righteous deeds.

{54} {Indeed, this is Our provision} — which We have bestowed upon the people of the abode of bliss — {it will never end}; that is, it will not cease, but rather it is permanent and established at all times, increasing at every moment. {And this is not great for the Lord, the Generous, the Compassionate, the Merciful, the Benevolent, the Bountiful, the Wide, the Rich, the Praiseworthy, the Subtle, the Most Merciful, the King, the Judge, the Majestic, the Beautiful, the Bestower, Possessor of overwhelming grace and continuous generosity, whose blessings cannot be counted and some of whose kindness cannot be encompassed.}

{56} Then He detailed it, saying: {Hell}, in which every kind of punishment has been gathered, whose heat is intense and whose coldness has ended, {they will burn in it}, that is, they will be tormented in it with a torment that encompasses them from every direction: {for them there will be canopies of fire above them and canopies beneath them}. {Wretched is the resting place}, that is, the place prepared for them as a dwelling and an abode.

{57} {This}: the resting place, this severe punishment, disgrace, humiliation and retribution. {Let them taste it: boiling water}, that is, water of intense heat, which they drink, and it cuts their intestines to pieces, {and ghassaq}: which is the most repugnant of drinks, made of pus and discharge, bitter in taste and foul in smell.

{58} {And other punishments of similar kind}, that is, of the same type, {in pairs}, that is, many categories of punishment, by which they will be tormented and disgraced.

{59–60} When they come upon the Fire one after another, some of them will revile others and say to one another: {This is a troop rushing in with you}, into the Fire. {No welcome for them! Indeed, they will burn in the Fire.} They will say, that is, the approaching troop rushing in: {Rather, it is you who have no welcome! You brought this upon us}, that is, the punishment, {through your calling us to it, your seduction of us, your misguidance of us and your causing it}. {Wretched is the abode}: the abode of all of them is an abode of evil and wrongdoing.

{61} Then they call down curses upon those who led them astray: {They will say: Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, add to him a double punishment in the Fire.} And in another verse He said: {He will say: For each there is double, but you do not know.}

{62} {And they will say}, while in the Fire: {What is the matter with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the wicked?}, that is, we used to claim that they were among the wicked deserving the punishment of the Fire, and they were the believers. The people of the Fire looked for them, may Allah curse them: do they see them in the Fire?

{63} {Did we take them in mockery, or have our eyes turned away from them?}, that is, our not seeing them is between two possibilities: either we were mistaken in counting them among the wicked, when in fact they were among the righteous, and our speech to them was only by way of mockery and ridicule, and this is the reality, as Allah the Exalted said to the people of the Fire: {Indeed, there was a group of My servants who said: Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the merciful. But you took them in mockery until they made you forget My remembrance, and you used to laugh at them.}
The second possibility: perhaps our eyes turned away from seeing them with us in the punishment, though in truth they are with us being punished, but our eyes passed over them. {65} {Say}: O Messenger, to these deniers, if they ask of you what is not yours and not in your hand: {I am only a warner}. This is the extent of what is with me. As for the command, it belongs to Allah, the Exalted. But I command you, forbid you, urge you toward good, and deter you from evil. Whoever is guided, it is for his own self; and whoever goes astray, it is against it. {There is no deity except Allah}; that is, no one truly deserves to be worshipped and taken as a god except Allah, {the One, the Subduer}. This establishes His divinity by this decisive proof, which is His oneness and His subjugation of everything. Subjugation necessarily entails oneness; there cannot be two equal subduers in their subjugation at all. The one who subdues all things is the One who has no equal, and He is the one who deserves to be worshipped alone, just as He is the sole Subduer.

{66} He also established this by the oneness of Lordship, saying: {Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them}; that is, their Creator, their Nurturer, and their Manager in every kind of management. {The Mighty}: who possesses the power by which He created the great creatures. {The Oft-Forgiving}: of all sins, small and great, for whoever repents to Him and abandons them. This is the One who is loved and who deserves to be worshipped, not those who create nothing, provide nothing, harm nothing, benefit nothing, and possess nothing of the affair, and who have no power of capability, and in whose hand is not the forgiveness of sins and burdens.

{67–68} {Say}: to them, as one who frightens, warns, rouses them, and gives warning: {It is a great news}; that is, what I have informed you of, concerning the Resurrection, the gathering, and the recompense for deeds, is a great report that deserves intense attention and must not be neglected. But {you turn away from it}: as though there were no reckoning, no punishment, and no reward before you.

{69–70} If you doubt my word and dispute my report, then I inform you of matters of which I have no knowledge and which I did not study from any book. My informing you of them exactly as they are, without addition or deficiency, is the greatest witness to my truthfulness and the strongest proof of the truth of what I have brought you. For this reason He said: {I had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly}; that is, the angels, {when they disputed}; were it not for Allah's teaching me and His revelation to me. For this reason He said: {It is only revealed to me that I am a plain warner}; that is, clearly evident in warning; there is no warner more eloquent than his warning, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.

{71–72} Then He mentioned the dispute of the Exalted Assembly, saying: {When your Lord said to the angels}, in the manner of informing: {Indeed, I am going to create a human from clay}; that is, its material is clay. {So when I have proportioned him}; that is, when I have formed his body and completed it, {and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down prostrate to him}.

{73–74} So the noble angels resolved themselves to this when his creation would be completed and the spirit breathed into him, in compliance with their Lord and in honor of Adam, peace be upon him. When his creation was complete in his body and spirit, and Allah tested Adam and the angels in knowledge and his superiority over them became evident, Allah commanded them to prostrate, and they prostrated, {all of them entirely, except Iblis}: he did not prostrate, {he was arrogant}: against the command of his Lord, and he was arrogant toward Adam, {and he was among the disbelievers}: in the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted.

{75} Allah said to him, rebuking and reproaching him: {What prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands}; that is, I honored him, ennobled him, and singled him out with this distinction in which he was specially favored over the rest of creation, and that requires not being arrogant toward him. {Have you become arrogant}: in your refusal, {or were you among the exalted?}

{76} {He said}: Iblis, opposing his Lord and contradicting Him: {I am better than him. You created me from fire and You created him from clay}. This is faulty analogy, for the element of fire is the substance of evil, corruption, haughtiness, recklessness, and lightness, whereas the element of clay is the substance of steadiness, humility, and the bringing forth of all kinds of trees and plants; it overcomes fire and extinguishes it, and fire needs a substance to sustain it while clay subsists by itself. This is the analogy of the chief of the people, who opposed the explicit command of Allah with it; its utter falsehood and corruption has been made clear. What then of the analogies of the students who opposed the truth with their analogies? All of them are far greater in falsehood and corruption than this analogy.

{79} {He said}: {My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected}: out of his intense enmity toward Adam and his descendants, so that he may be able to mislead whomever Allah has decreed he will mislead.

{80–81} So {He said}, Allah responding to his supplication, as His wisdom required that: {Indeed, you are of those reprieved, until the Day of the time made known}: when the offspring are completed and the trial is finished.

{82–83} When he knew that he was reprieved, he displayed from his wickedness the intensity of his enmity toward his Lord, toward Adam, and toward his descendants, and said: {By Your might, I will surely mislead them all entirely}. It is possible that the "ba" is for oath, and that he swore by the might of Allah that he would mislead them all entirely, {except for Your sincere servants among them}: he knew that Allah would protect them from his plotting. It is also possible that the "ba" is for seeking help, and that, knowing he was utterly powerless, and that he misleads no one except by the will of Allah, the Exalted, he sought help through the might of Allah to mislead the descendants of Adam. This is the enemy of Allah in truth, while we, O our Lord, are the powerless and deficient, acknowledging before You every blessing, the descendants of the one You have honored and ennobled. So we seek help through Your great might, Your power, and Your vast mercy toward every creature, and Your mercy by which You have brought us what You have brought of religious and worldly blessings and turned away from us what You have turned away of calamities: that You help us to fight him, to oppose his enmity, and to be safe from his evil and his shirk. We have called upon You as You commanded us, so respond to us as You promised us. {Indeed, You do not fail in promise}.

{84–85} {He said}, Allah the Exalted: {So the truth is, and the truth I say}; that is, the truth is My attribute and the truth is My speech: {I will surely fill Hell with you and those of them who follow you, all together}.

{86} When the Messenger had made the proof clear to the people and shown them the path, Allah said to him: {Say, "I do not ask you for any payment for it"}; that is, for my calling you, {and I am not of the pretenders}: claiming a matter that is not mine, and pursuing what I have no knowledge of. I follow only what is revealed to me.

{87} {It is not except a reminder to the worlds}; that is, this revelation and the Qur'an, by which they remember everything that benefits them in the interests of their religion and their worldly life, so that it becomes an honor and an elevation for the worlds through it, and a establishment of proof against the obstinate.

This great surah includes the Wise Reminder, the great news, the establishment of proofs and evidences against whoever denies the Qur'an, opposes it, and denies the one who brought it, and the report of the sincere servants of Allah and the recompense of the righteous and the transgressors. For this reason He swore at its beginning that it is full of reminder, described it at its end as a reminder to the worlds, and repeated the call to remembrance within it, as in His saying: {And remember Our servant}, {And remember Our servants}, {A mercy from Us and a reminder}, {This is a reminder}. O Allah, teach us what we do not know of it, and remind us of what we have forgotten of it, forgetfulness of heedlessness and forgetfulness of abandonment.

{88} {And you will surely know its news}; that is, its report, {after a time}: and that is when the punishment befalls them and the means are cut off from them.

Here ends the tafsir of Surah Sad, by the grace and help of Allah, the Exalted.
